groups.title: Monadic and dyadic possessive formulas
groups.proposal: Build a possessive-state NNC with either a one-part or two-part possessor position while reusing the Lesson 12 subject-person morphs.
groups.writingJob: Preserve the typed subject, possessor, nounstem predicate, State, and formula boundaries in both possessive formulas.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in recognizing whether the possessor position is monadic or dyadic without confusing it with the subject.
groups.decisionSplit: The intended possessor determines the formula; the application chooses the proper structure and reuses the subject morphs.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Possessor and State; do not add a monadic/dyadic picker.

groups.title: Possessive-state subject connectors and paradigm
groups.proposal: Generate every possessive-state subject form from person, number, nounstem boundary, and typed morphological conditioning.
groups.writingJob: Select uh, hu, hui, zero, and ān automatically and generate the complete possessive-state subject paradigm.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in identifying supportive i, silent versus sounded following morphs, and possessive-only subject shapes.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses subject person and number; the application selects every connector and spelling realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Subject and Full paradigm; never expose connector morphs as choices.

groups.title: Reciprocal and nonspecific possessors
groups.proposal: Build monadic possessors ne, tē, and tla from their real meanings and restrictions.
groups.writingJob: Generate reciprocal, nonspecific-human, or nonspecific-nonhuman possession and enforce third-person and relational restrictions where required.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in distinguishing reciprocal possession from reflexive-reciprocal objects and human from nonhuman nonspecific possession.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended possessor meaning; the application chooses the morph and enforces applicability.
groups.controlPolicy: Use the existing Possessor choice; show only meanings available for the current nounstem and subject.

groups.title: Dyadic possessor person and number structure
groups.proposal: Build the first possessor subposition from person, number, and possessive case according to the possessor's person.
groups.writingJob: Generate ī for third-person possessors and n, t, m, or am for first- and second-person possessors.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in seeing which categories are carried by the first possessor subposition.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the possessor; the application distributes person, number, and case across the two subpositions.

groups.title: Dyadic second subposition and vowel-initial replacement
groups.proposal: Complete the dyadic possessor with third-person number or first/second-person possessive case.
groups.writingJob: Generate zero, m or n for third-person number and automatically replace possessive o with its irregular mate before a vowel-initial nounstem.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in recognizing the category supplied by the second subposition and the vowel-initial replacement.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses possessor and nounstem; the application supplies the second morph and its boundary-conditioned form.
groups.controlPolicy: No new control; plural m/n is exposed only if both are genuinely authorized results.

groups.title: Specific possessor paradigm and reading distinction
groups.proposal: Generate the complete specific possessor paradigm while preserving the difference between amo and ammo structures.
groups.writingJob: Generate every specific possessor form and keep the NNC second-plural possessor distinct from the VNC second-plural reflexive sequence.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through possessor translations, broader plural readings, and ambiguous traditional spelling.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the possessor; the application generates its form, while sentence structure resolves visually ambiguous spelling.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Possessor and Full paradigm; no spelling-disambiguation control.
